issues.description: The type of StockIngredient.price is inconsistent across artifacts. The problem statement's UML and method signatures (acceptSupplyDelivery(String, int, int) and calculateTotalPrice returning int) expect an integer price. The solution implements StockIngredient.price as an int, but the template's StockIngredient defines price as a double (constructor and getPrice use double). This mismatch will confuse students when they implement SealSaloon.acceptSupplyDelivery(String, int, int) and try to create new StockIngredient instances (constructor expects double in the template) or sum prices into an int result as required by the specification.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the price type consistent. Either change the template's StockIngredient.price (and its constructor/getPrice) from double to int so it matches the problem UML and the solution, or update the problem statement and solution to use double everywhere (including acceptSupplyDelivery parameter type and calculateTotalPrice return type). The recommended fix is to update the template StockIngredient to use int for price (constructor parameter and getPrice return type) to match the problem specification and the solution.
